concepts.why: The presence of multiple, iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous humor is consistent with Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1.
The patient's morning glory optic disc anomaly and low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina are characteristic of this condition.
The patient's chronic retinal detachment is a known complication of morning glory disc anomaly.
The patient's spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage are consistent with traumatic injury to the eye.
The patient's vitreous hemorrhage is a known complication of traumatic eye injury.
The presence of iridescent crystals in the aqueous humor may be associated with glaucoma.
The presence of iridescent crystals in the aqueous humor may be associated with uveitis.
The patient's chronic retinal detachment may be associated with retinal dialysis.
